SCI-SPK-F00-Q01.text: Listen to the word, then say it back clearly.

SCI-SPK-F00-Q02.text: What is in this picture? Say the word out loud.

SCI-SPK-F00-Q03.text: Have a look at the picture and say its name.

SCI-SPK-F00-Q04.text: There's a word on the screen. Read it out loud for me.

SCI-SPK-F00-Q05.text: When you know what this picture shows, say the word out loud.

SCI-SPK-F00-Q06.text: Listen carefully to the question, then say your answer out loud.

SCI-SPK-F00-Q07.text: Take a look at the picture. What do you see? Say it out loud.

SCI-SPK-F00-Q08.text: Look at the picture, then say the word for what you see.

SCI-SPK-T01-Q01.text: Listen to the science word, then say it back as clearly as you can.

SCI-SPK-T01-Q02.text: You'll hear a science word in a moment. Listen closely, then repeat it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T01-Q03.text: Ready to listen? A science word is coming. When you've heard it, say it back.

SCI-SPK-T01-Q04.text: Pay close attention to the word you hear, then say it back. Go slowly if you like.

SCI-SPK-T01-Q05.text: Here comes a science word. Listen, then say it out loud just the way you heard it.

SCI-SPK-T01-Q06.text: Listen like a scientist collecting sounds. Then say the word back clearly.

SCI-SPK-T01-Q07.text: This word can be tricky to say. Listen closely, then have a go at saying it back.

SCI-SPK-T01-Q08.text: Can you say the word back, sound by sound? Listen carefully first.

SCI-SPK-T01-Q09.text: Big word alert. Listen carefully, then try saying it back one chunk at a time.

SCI-SPK-T01-Q10.text: Imagine you're a parrot in a science lab. Listen to the word, then say it right back.

SCI-SPK-T02-Q01.text: Look at the picture. What is it? Say its name out loud.

SCI-SPK-T02-Q02.text: Can you tell me what this picture shows? Say it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T02-Q03.text: What do you see in the picture? Say the word clearly.

SCI-SPK-T02-Q04.text: Study the picture for a moment. When you know what it shows, say its name.

SCI-SPK-T02-Q05.text: Name what you see. Look at the picture, then say the word out loud.

SCI-SPK-T02-Q06.text: Here's a picture for you. Say the science word for what it shows.

SCI-SPK-T02-Q07.text: What's in this picture? Have a good look, then say what it is.

SCI-SPK-T02-Q08.text: Take a close look at the picture, then say the name of what you see.

SCI-SPK-T02-Q09.text: Science lab time. Look at the picture and say what it's called.

SCI-SPK-T02-Q10.text: Imagine you found this in a science kit. What is it? Say its name out loud.

SCI-SPK-T03-Q01.text: Imagine a dog is waiting at the door for you. What sound does it make? Make that sound out loud.

SCI-SPK-T03-Q02.text: What sound does a cat make? Have a go at making it.

SCI-SPK-T03-Q03.text: Off to the farm. There is a cow in the field. What sound does a cow make? Say it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T03-Q04.text: A duck is paddling across the pond. What sound does it make? Let's hear you do it.

SCI-SPK-T03-Q05.text: An owl is sitting in a tree at night. What sound does an owl make? Try it.

SCI-SPK-T03-Q06.text: A bee is flying around the flowers. Can you make the sound a bee makes?

SCI-SPK-T03-Q07.text: Picture a snake sliding through the grass. What sound does a snake make? Make it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T03-Q08.text: Think of a sheep in a green field. What sound does it make? Say it for me.

SCI-SPK-T03-Q09.text: Deep in the forest, there is a wolf. What sound does a wolf make? Have a go.

SCI-SPK-T03-Q10.text: An elephant is standing at the watering hole. What sound does an elephant make? Make it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T04-Q01.text: There's a science word on the screen. Read it out loud in your clearest voice.

SCI-SPK-T04-Q02.text: Can you read the word on the screen? Say it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T04-Q03.text: Read the word to yourself first, then say it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T04-Q04.text: Say the word on the screen out loud, clearly enough for me to hear every sound.

SCI-SPK-T04-Q05.text: Look at each letter of the word on the screen. Sound it out if you need to, then read it aloud.

SCI-SPK-T04-Q06.text: Take a look at this word. When you are ready, read it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T04-Q07.text: This word has a few parts. Read it carefully, then say the whole thing out loud.

SCI-SPK-T04-Q08.text: What does the word on the screen say? Read it out loud for me.

SCI-SPK-T04-Q09.text: Big word challenge. Break the word on the screen into chunks, then read the whole thing out loud.

SCI-SPK-T04-Q10.text: Imagine you're a scientist sharing a new word with your class. Read the word on the screen out loud.

SCI-SPK-T05-Q01.text: There's a science sentence on the screen. Read it out loud, nice and clearly.

SCI-SPK-T05-Q02.text: Can you read the sentence on the screen out loud? Take your time.

SCI-SPK-T05-Q03.text: First read the sentence to yourself. Then read it out loud in a steady voice.

SCI-SPK-T05-Q04.text: Look at each word in the sentence, then read the whole thing aloud.

SCI-SPK-T05-Q05.text: This sentence is a bit longer. Read it out loud from start to finish, without rushing.

SCI-SPK-T05-Q06.text: Read the sentence on the screen out loud. If a word is tricky, slow down and sound it out.

SCI-SPK-T05-Q07.text: Here's a sentence with some science words in it. Read it aloud as clearly as you can.

SCI-SPK-T05-Q08.text: Take a breath, then read the sentence on the screen out loud at a comfortable pace.

SCI-SPK-T05-Q09.text: Long sentence ahead. Read it out loud one part at a time, all the way to the end.

SCI-SPK-T05-Q10.text: Imagine you're the narrator of a nature film. Read the sentence on the screen out loud.

SCI-SPK-T06-Q01.text: What do you know about fish? Tell me one fact, in your own words.

SCI-SPK-T06-Q02.text: Think about plants. Say one thing you know about them.

SCI-SPK-T06-Q03.text: Share a fact about the sun. It can be anything you know, as long as it's true.

SCI-SPK-T06-Q04.text: What's one fact you know about your body? Say it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T06-Q05.text: Tell me something you know about bees. One fact is plenty.

SCI-SPK-T06-Q06.text: Volcanoes are your topic. What is one fact you could share about them? Say it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T06-Q07.text: Say one fact you know about butterflies, in your own words.

SCI-SPK-T06-Q08.text: Dolphins: what's something you know about them? Tell me one fact.

SCI-SPK-T06-Q09.text: Let's talk about the water cycle. Say one fact you know about it.

SCI-SPK-T06-Q10.text: Imagine you're teaching a friend about the scientific method. What's one fact you'd tell them? Say it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T07-Q01.text: Think about a dog. Which group does it belong to? Say the group, and tell me why.

SCI-SPK-T07-Q02.text: What group would you put an apple in? Say your answer and explain why.

SCI-SPK-T07-Q03.text: Which group does a rock belong to, and what makes you think so? Say it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T07-Q04.text: Where does a rose belong? Name a group for it and give your reason.

SCI-SPK-T07-Q05.text: Think carefully about a whale. Which group does it fit into, and why? Explain out loud.

SCI-SPK-T07-Q06.text: Say which group a lion belongs to. Then tell me what makes it fit there.

SCI-SPK-T07-Q07.text: What group does ice belong to? Say your answer, and explain your thinking.

SCI-SPK-T07-Q08.text: Which group would you sort a frog into? Say the group and give a reason.

SCI-SPK-T07-Q09.text: Imagine you're sorting food in a science kitchen. Where does a tomato belong, and why? Say it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T07-Q10.text: A bat: which group does it belong to? Tell me, and explain why.

SCI-SPK-T08-Q01.text: Look at the pictures. Describe what's happening, using science words if you can.

SCI-SPK-T08-Q02.text: What do you notice in these pictures? Describe it out loud with some science words.

SCI-SPK-T08-Q03.text: Study the pictures like a scientist. Then describe what you see, using science words.

SCI-SPK-T08-Q04.text: Have a good look at the pictures. Tell me what they show, using the best science words you know.

SCI-SPK-T08-Q05.text: Describe this scene out loud, and try to use science words as you go.

SCI-SPK-T08-Q06.text: What's going on in these pictures? Describe it, and use science words where you can.

SCI-SPK-T08-Q07.text: Go through the pictures in order. Describe what you see, using science words.

SCI-SPK-T08-Q08.text: Describe what you see here, the way a scientist would in their notes. Use science words.

SCI-SPK-T08-Q09.text: There is a lot going on in these pictures. Describe what you see from start to finish, using science words.

SCI-SPK-T08-Q10.text: Imagine you're telling a story about these pictures. Describe what's happening, using science words.

SCI-SPK-T09-Q01.text: Think about an elephant and a mouse. Which one is bigger? Say your answer in a full sentence.

SCI-SPK-T09-Q02.text: Picture a snail and a rabbit having a race. Which one is faster? Tell me out loud.

SCI-SPK-T09-Q03.text: A feather and a brick. If you held one in each hand, which would be heavier? Say it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T09-Q04.text: Compare a mountain and a hill. Which one is taller? Say your answer.

SCI-SPK-T09-Q05.text: Here's a tougher one: a whale and an elephant. Which is bigger? Say it in a sentence.

SCI-SPK-T09-Q06.text: Ice and boiling water. Which one is hotter? Tell me out loud.

SCI-SPK-T09-Q07.text: Imagine a cheetah and a tortoise on a running track. Which one is faster? Say your answer.

SCI-SPK-T09-Q08.text: You have a bucket and a cup. Which one holds more? Say it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T09-Q09.text: Number puzzle time. Work out half of 10, then a quarter of 20. How do they compare? Say what you find.

SCI-SPK-T09-Q10.text: Imagine a blue whale, an elephant and a horse standing in a line. Which one is the biggest of all? Say your answer.

SCI-SPK-T10-Q01.text: The pictures show how a butterfly grows. Tell it in order, from the very first stage to the last.

SCI-SPK-T10-Q02.text: These pictures show a plant growing. Can you talk through each step in order? Use words like first, then and next.

SCI-SPK-T10-Q03.text: Use the weather pictures to explain what happens, step by step, in the right order.

SCI-SPK-T10-Q04.text: The pictures show how a frog grows up. Say each stage in order, using words like first and then.

SCI-SPK-T10-Q05.text: These pictures show a volcano in action. Talk through the whole process in the right order.

SCI-SPK-T10-Q06.text: How does a cut heal? Use the pictures to tell me the steps in order, from start to finish.

SCI-SPK-T10-Q07.text: Follow a bee's busy day in the pictures. Describe what happens in order, step by step.

SCI-SPK-T10-Q08.text: Follow water on its journey. Use the pictures to tell each step in order.

SCI-SPK-T10-Q09.text: Imagine you're a scientist explaining how you work. Use the pictures to say each step in order.

SCI-SPK-T10-Q10.text: These pictures follow energy from the sun. Can you tell each step in order, from start to finish?

SCI-SPK-T11-Q01.text: Imagine putting a tray of water in the freezer and leaving it overnight. What do you think you'll find in the morning? Say your prediction.

SCI-SPK-T11-Q02.text: A seed is planted, and it gets water and sunlight every day. What do you predict will happen? Tell me out loud.

SCI-SPK-T11-Q03.text: Picture a plant shut away in a completely dark cupboard for two weeks. What do you predict will happen to it?

SCI-SPK-T11-Q04.text: Two identical ice cubes: one in a warm room, one in the fridge. What do you predict will happen? Explain your prediction.

SCI-SPK-T11-Q05.text: A caterpillar has been eating a huge amount of leaves for weeks. What do you think will happen next? Say your prediction.

SCI-SPK-T11-Q06.text: A lunchbox with meat inside is left in a hot car all day. What do you predict will happen to the food?

SCI-SPK-T11-Q07.text: A scientist adds special fertiliser to just one of two identical plants. What do you predict will happen? Say what you think.

SCI-SPK-T11-Q08.text: Scientists have noticed ice at the poles getting thinner every year, while ocean temperatures rise. What do you predict could happen next?

SCI-SPK-T11-Q09.text: Imagine a new kind of plant arrives by accident on an island with no natural predators for it. What do you predict will happen over time?

SCI-SPK-T11-Q10.text: Two identical plants: one is watered every day, the other only once a week. What do you predict will happen? Say your idea.

SCI-SPK-T12-Q01.text: Think about an ice cube in a warm room. Why does it melt? Explain your thinking out loud.

SCI-SPK-T12-Q02.text: When a plant goes without water, it wilts. Why do you think that happens? Explain out loud.

SCI-SPK-T12-Q03.text: A glass is dropped on a hard floor and it breaks. Why does that happen? Talk me through your reasons.

SCI-SPK-T12-Q04.text: Here's one to puzzle over. Why does shaking a fizzy drink bottle make it spray out fast when the cap comes off? Explain what you think.

SCI-SPK-T12-Q05.text: When bees visit flowers, it helps plants make seeds. Why do you think that is? Explain in your own words.

SCI-SPK-T12-Q06.text: Why is it risky to leave meat in a hot car all day? Say what you think and why.

SCI-SPK-T12-Q07.text: A caterpillar eats a lot before it forms a cocoon. Why does it need so much food? Explain your idea.

SCI-SPK-T12-Q08.text: Imagine a whole forest is cut down. Why might that affect animals that don't even live in the trees? Explain your thinking.

SCI-SPK-T12-Q09.text: Picture a team of scientists with a new medicine. Why do they test it on many people, not just one, before deciding it works? Explain out loud.

SCI-SPK-T12-Q10.text: When scientists design a test, they change only one thing at a time. Why do you think they do that? Explain.

SCI-SPK-T13-Q01.text: Look at the butterfly. What do you wonder about it? Ask a science question out loud.

SCI-SPK-T13-Q02.text: Here's a volcano. If you could ask a scientist one question about it, what would it be? Say your question.

SCI-SPK-T13-Q03.text: Think about the moon. What's a science question you'd like answered? Ask it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T13-Q04.text: What would you like to find out about this bee? Ask your question out loud.

SCI-SPK-T13-Q05.text: Come up with a science question about dolphins. Make it something you'd really like to know.

SCI-SPK-T13-Q06.text: Look at the ice. What could you investigate about it? Ask a science question out loud.

SCI-SPK-T13-Q07.text: Rainbows can make us wonder. What science question do you have about them? Ask it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T13-Q08.text: Think about an owl. What's one science question you could ask about it? Say it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T13-Q09.text: Picture ice melting at the poles. What science question pops into your head? Ask it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T13-Q10.text: Imagine you're planning a fair scientific test. What science question would you want to ask about it? Say it out loud.

SCI-SPK-T14-Q01.text: How could you find out if plants need sunlight to grow? Explain the test you would do.

SCI-SPK-T14-Q02.text: Say how you would test whether ice melts faster in warm places. Talk me through your plan.

SCI-SPK-T14-Q03.text: Imagine you've made a few paper planes. How would you test which design flies furthest? Explain your plan.

SCI-SPK-T14-Q04.text: Does music affect how fast a plant grows? How would you test it? Explain your idea out loud.

SCI-SPK-T14-Q05.text: You want to know which type of soil grows the tallest bean plant. How would you test it? Describe your plan.

SCI-SPK-T14-Q06.text: Warm water or cold water: which freezes faster? Instead of guessing, explain how you would test it.

SCI-SPK-T14-Q07.text: How would you test whether a certain fertiliser really helps plants grow better? Explain your steps.

SCI-SPK-T14-Q08.text: Imagine you're in charge of testing a new medicine. How would you check it actually works, in a way scientists would trust? Explain your plan.

SCI-SPK-T14-Q09.text: A gardener wonders if bees are really needed for the flowers to produce fruit. How would you test it? Explain.

SCI-SPK-T14-Q10.text: Does background noise affect how well people concentrate? How would you test it? Talk through your plan.

SCI-SPK-T15-Q01.text: Let's investigate whether plants need sunlight to grow. Talk through your whole investigation, from the question to what you'd look for at the end.

SCI-SPK-T15-Q02.text: Your investigation: does ice melt faster in warm places? Walk me through it from start to finish.

SCI-SPK-T15-Q03.text: Does the amount of water affect how tall a plant grows? Plan the whole investigation out loud, step by step.

SCI-SPK-T15-Q04.text: Do bees prefer some flower colours over others? Talk through how you'd investigate this, start to finish.

SCI-SPK-T15-Q05.text: Think about paper planes. Does the shape of one affect how far it flies? Describe your whole investigation, beginning to end.

SCI-SPK-T15-Q06.text: Here's a big one: does salty water freeze at the same temperature as plain water? Talk through your full investigation.

SCI-SPK-T15-Q07.text: Investigation time. Does the size of an ice cube affect how quickly it melts? Tell me your whole plan, from start to finish.

SCI-SPK-T15-Q08.text: Imagine you're a plant scientist. Does a plant grow better with tap water or bottled water? Talk through your investigation.

SCI-SPK-T15-Q09.text: Does background noise affect how quickly someone solves a simple puzzle? How would you investigate? Talk it through from start to finish.

SCI-SPK-T15-Q10.text: Picture a garden full of plants. Do they all need the same amount of sunlight, or do some need more shade? Talk through your whole investigation.
